I’ve always been a bit of a worrier, but over the past few months it feels like my brain is stuck on overdrive. At work, when I’m on the console, I’m supposed to be locked in on one caller, one screen, but my mind keeps jumping: “What if I miss something? What if I say the wrong thing? What if something happens and it’s my fault?” It’s like I’m constantly running through worst-case scenarios, and once that starts, I can’t shut it off, even when I’m off shift.

I’ve tried all the usual things—podcasts, music, scrolling my phone, going for walks—but the worry just keeps circling back. I’ll catch myself rereading the same line in an email three times because I can’t hold my focus. Even in conversations, I sort of zone out halfway through and realize I’ve missed chunks of what people are saying.

The job doesn’t help. Some of the calls I’ve taken still replay in my head sometimes, especially a couple of really bad ones, but I’m not sure if this all started because of that or if it just kind of built up over time. I just know I can’t seem to get my mind to settle.
D011-D018_h023.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D011-D018_h023.answer: D & C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D011-D018_h024.question:
I’ve been on edge for at least the past six, maybe eight months. It’s like my mind never shuts up. I’m constantly going over things—work details, my bills, my health, whether I missed something—over and over. Even when I tell myself, “Enough, it’s fine,” it just keeps circling back, and I can’t seem to switch it off.

On a job I’m supposed to be fully locked in, watching hands, exits, body language. Lately my focus keeps slipping. I’ll be staring at a doorway, then realize my head drifted off into “what if” stuff—what if I messed up last week, what if something happens to the client, what if I don’t notice something. Then I get annoyed with myself for losing focus, which just makes me more wound up.

There was an incident on a detail a while back—things got messy—and since then I feel like the volume’s been turned up on all this. I don’t know if it started exactly then or was building before, but since that job I’ve been more on guard, even off duty. I try TV, the gym, talking to guys from work, but the worrying just pushes back in.
D011-D018_h024.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D011-D018_h024.answer: D & C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D011-D018_h025.question:
I’ve always been a bit of a worrier, but over the last few months it feels like it’s taken over. It’s not just one thing—I’m worrying about everything all at once. At work I’m constantly running through “what ifs”: what if I mess up an order, what if someone gets sick, what if we lose business and I can’t support my wife. On my days off I’m stressing about bills, my parents getting older, whether something might happen to my wife on her commute, even random stuff like the gas stove leaking.

It feels like my brain won’t shut up. I’ll try to focus on prep or following a ticket, and suddenly I’m stuck in my head running through worst‑case scenarios instead of paying attention to the pan in front of me. I know it doesn’t make sense, and I tell myself to stop, but the thoughts just keep coming back. I’ll try deep breaths, music, whatever, and maybe it helps for a minute, then it all ramps up again.

There was an incident at the restaurant a while back that shook me up, but I’m not sure how much that ties into all this. I just know this constant worrying is starting to wear me down.
D011-D018_h025.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D011-D018_h025.answer: D & C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
